comment: Every released shape of the booking storage contract, oldest first. The last entry must match bookingSchemaHash(prisma/schema.prisma); a release that changes a Booking* model adds an entry here or the build refuses it. bookingAdditive says the named migration leaves the previous entry's artifact able to keep serving — only added nullable booking columns, proven against the migration SQL by release-contract.test.mjs. It is a claim about the booking storage contract alone.

releases.note: The canonical booking backend and the one-time workspace activation. Baseline: the first released shape, so it claims nothing about anything before it.
A salon service carries a price, the currency it was stamped in, a group and a return cycle: four nullable columns on booking_pages.
What a single master charges for a service and how long they take: one nullable JSON column on booking_pages. A release that does not know it reads every page exactly as before.
Extras a customer may add to a service, each with its own price and minutes: one nullable JSON column on booking_pages. A release that does not know it serves every page as before.
A picture of the service on its public page: one nullable column on booking_pages holding a path under /uploads/booking-photos.
How many customers take a service together: one NOT NULL column with a default of 1 on booking_pages, so an older writer's rows read as one at a time.
